status_note: Launched 2026-08-11T18:07Z on av2 and av3, both hosts complete by 2026-08-12T03:48Z, collected and closed 2026-08-12. Every field here is read from the launch record, the per-host manifests, the CSV itself or the retained run directories; nothing is inferred from an mtime except the per-host run window, which is labelled as such.
kind_note: A standard gen_configs.py / run_experiments.py / merge_experiments.py TLSF repair campaign, and the first driven end to end by scripts/campaign.py (stage / start / status / collect) rather than by an agent holding the state. The only factor is fitness.status_grading, carried by TLSF sweep G. Both arms of a (spec, seed) pair run on the same host, which is what makes a host difference cancel inside the pair the endpoints are measured over.
question: Whether the status objective should grade the region below realizability at all. The shipped scale was three-point -- 0 for a component unsatisfiable on its own, 0.5 for everything unrealizable, 1.0 for realizable and well-separated -- so the entire unrealizable region, which is where the search spends nearly all of its time, was one flat value and offered selection no gradient. `mrs` replaces the middle tier with the fraction of guarantee-side parts a greedy sweep keeps realizable against the unchanged environment side. Prior work on counterstrategy volume as the gradient failed structurally rather than for want of tuning, so the question is whether a subset-fraction gradient does what a counting one could not. See the volume-metrics caveat below.
decision: Default fitness.status_grading to mrs. Yield 410/480 against tiered's 367/480 -- paired, 50 mrs-only against 7 tiered-only, sign test p < 0.0001 -- with repair quality unchanged on the 360 pairs where both arms yield (mrs better on 3, tiered on 2, mean implies_ideal delta +0.0028), at a median paired wall cost of 1.15x. Almost all of the gain is on two specifications tiered grades as a single flat value: arbiter 0/24 -> 22/24 and rg1 7/24 -> 24/24.
decision_rule: None was pre-registered, deliberately. PLAN.md section 5 sets out why: the campaign is the first measurement of a scale the search had never had, so there was no prior sharp enough to name a threshold that would not have been chosen after seeing the shape of the answer. The endpoints, their pairing and the direction that would count as an improvement were all registered before any row at this commit was collected; the cut was not. Read the decision above as a judgement on registered evidence, not as a rule firing.

engine_commits_this_campaign_depends_on.why: adds the mrs grading itself -- status_score_mrs, the TLSF guarantee-part split, and the fitness.status_grading key the sweep varies

guards the NSGA-II crowding infinities on zero range. Load-bearing here rather than incidental: the unfixed code pinned two arbitrary members of a front above every finitely-scored one whenever an objective had zero range, and a flat objective is exactly what the tiered arm makes status. Leaving it in would have given the tiered arm a selection defect the mrs arm largely escapes, and charged the difference to the grading scale.

raises the ltlsynt budget from 500 ms to 10 s and screens the input specification's own query at startup. Also load-bearing: at 500 ms amba's own realizability query could not be decided at all, and an undecided query resolves as unrealizable everywhere including the final gate, so amba's archived 96/96 zero-yield measured the budget rather than the search.

raises TLSF_LTLSYNT_TIMEOUT_MS in gen_configs.py, which a generated TLSF campaign emits explicitly and which therefore overrides the C++ default above. Changing one without the other fixes nothing for a campaign.

merge_experiments_exception.why: This one copy is NOT from the profile commit, and deliberately so. At 8d21266 the profile was registered in run_experiments.PROFILES but not in merge_experiments.PROFILE_CSVS / PROFILE_RESULT_DIRS, which is the table campaign.py collect resolves a profile against -- so collection refused outright and the merge could not have run at 8d21266. 5c3f7b8 adds the two entries and changes nothing else. Vendoring the copy that actually merged the rows is the honest record; vendoring the profile-commit copy would name a file that cannot perform the step it is filed under. The runs themselves are untouched by this and still carry commit=8d21266 in every row.

analysis_scripts.note: Written after the campaign to read the merged CSV, so this is not a vendored driver copy and carries no source_commit. It evaluates the three registered endpoints and the two supplementary breakdowns quoted in the caveats below.

design.sweep_note: A sweep rather than a crossed factor, and that choice is load-bearing. A new factor would have joined KEY_FIELDS in merge_experiments.py, and the ~225k archived result rows carry no such column -- so every one of them would have missed its resume key and re-run a finished campaign. Sweep G rides the existing level_name column instead.
design.scheme: nsga2-truncate only, not crossed; it is the shipped default and the question is about the shipped configuration
design.jobs_note: jobs=1 for the same RAM reason as every other TLSF profile: max_concurrent_realizability is a per-process cap, so a second concurrent counter process doubles the peak ltlsynt residency rather than sharing a ceiling
design.timeout_caps: Per spec rather than the flat 600 s of ablate-tlsf, and recalibrated for this campaign: amba 4320 s, humanoid-531 1560, lift 840, simple-arbiter 720, round-robin-arbiter 660, humanoid-458 540, full-arbiter / gyro-var1 / gyro-var2 420, detector 360, the remaining ten 300. Sized from a 120-row pilot sweep at the raised ltlsynt budget, to at least 4x the pilot's worst observed wall time per spec. The flat cap could not be kept: raising the ltlsynt budget lets a query run up to 20x longer than the old caps assumed, and amba's mrs arm alone measured 1078 s standalone, so 600 s would have censored the expensive arm and returned the censoring as a result.
design.config_deviation_from_shipped_defaults: gen_configs.py's baseline pins the fitness weights at 0.33/0.33/0.1/0.33 rather than config.hpp's 0.2/0.5/0.1/0.5, plus model_counting.default_bound = 20 and runtime.black_timeout_ms = 1000, and TLSF_LTLSYNT_TIMEOUT_MS = 10000. These are campaign conventions shared with the prior TLSF sweeps; changing them here would make this campaign incomparable with them. Under nsga2-truncate the weights select which components are active rather than how they trade, so they do not bias selection between the arms.

host_split.method: seed-major, disjoint, never by spec or arm -- so both arms of every (spec, seed) pair run on the same host, and a host lost mid-campaign still leaves a balanced design over every spec and arm
host_split.hostname_note: The per-host manifest filename uses the machine's real hostname rather than the ssh alias, so av2's manifest is results-status-grading-manifest-avlab12.json
host_split.host_asymmetry: av2 carries a llama-server on one of its 32 cores. It cannot bias the comparison, because pairing is within host; a pilot put the two hosts within 3.4% on a 93 s run.

run_window.per_host_source: oldest and newest run.log mtime under the campaign's results directory, read on each host's own clock. These are mtimes and are labelled as such -- they bound the window rather than record it, since the first log appears only once the first run writes.
run_window.clock_note: av2 and av3 both returned 2026-08-12T12:17:16Z to a `date -u` issued sequentially at collection time, so their clocks agree to within a second. The ~17 minute av3 skew recorded against earlier campaigns does not apply here. No figure in this campaign derives from a cross-host timestamp in any case: wall_time_s is measured per run by the host that ran it, and every comparison is within a host.
run_window.false_start: launches.jsonl records two launches per host, at 19:04 and 19:07 local. The 19:04 pair exited immediately and wrote no rows: campaign.py stages the checkout but never runs gen_configs.py, and experiments/configs-* is gitignored, so both hosts had the code and no configs. Configs were generated on each host and the campaign relaunched. The dead launch is left in the record rather than edited out.

caveats: The extra yield is repairs, not ideal-matching repairs. Of the 50 mrs-only pairs, 43 score implies_ideal = 0 -- realizable weakenings the reference fix does not imply. Seven are non-zero: five of arbiter's 22, one on simple-arbiter and one on lily02, the last at 1.000. Quote the 410/480 as yield and this split alongside it; the two together are the honest statement.

Repair quality is unchanged rather than improved. Over the whole 480 pairs the quality endpoint reads 10-2 to mrs at p = 0.0386, but that test counts a pair where only one arm yielded as a quality difference, which is endpoint 1 counted twice. Restricted to the 360 pairs where both arms yielded it is 3-2 with a mean delta of +0.0028 -- no detectable difference either way. The campaign shows mrs buys yield without costing quality; it does not show mrs improves quality.

Aggregate cost overstates the typical cost, and the median understates the worst. The median paired ratio is 1.15x and the aggregate is 1.89x (12.20 h against 6.45 h); the gap is amba, at 4.52x. Per spec the range runs from 0.92x -- simple-arbiter, where mrs is faster -- to that 4.52x. Do not size a cap table, a schedule or a cost claim from any single spec's ratio.

Two specifications carry the yield result. arbiter (0/24 -> 22/24) and rg1 (7/24 -> 24/24) supply 39 of the 50 mrs-only pairs. Fourteen of the twenty specifications are exactly tied. The finding is that mrs reaches a family tiered cannot grade, not that it lifts the corpus uniformly, and a corpus with a different share of that family would move the headline rate.
One specification regresses: minepump 17/24 -> 15/24, two pairs. Unexplained, and too small to separate from noise at this n.
prioritized-arbiter yields zero in both arms, 0/24 each. It contributes a denominator and nothing else.

Censoring is negligible but not zero: one timed_out row per arm out of 480 (mrs on full-arbiter, tiered on lift), and no compare_timed_out rows at all. The recalibrated caps held with margin on both arms, so neither arm is flattered by censoring.

The campaign says nothing about the FRETISH path. Both the grading and the guarantee-part split are implemented on both paths, but only TLSF was run; the FRETISH corpus and operating point differ enough that the ratio and the yield gain should not be carried across.

The campaign says nothing about counterstrategy volume as an alternative gradient. That approach was ruled out structurally beforehand rather than by this measurement, and no arm here tests it. The reason it fails is a property of the metric class rather than of any implementation: on the arbiter family the guarantee is a liveness one, the input words that defeat it are measure-zero under a uniform measure, and every bounded prefix extends to a satisfying trace -- so both prefix counting and uniform measure read 1.0 for every candidate, however far from realizable it is. A gradient cannot be recovered by tuning a metric that is constant. That is also why mrs was reached for: it counts guarantee-side parts, which is a syntactic quantity a liveness/safety distinction cannot flatten.

Both arms ran with run_well_separation at its current default and allow_output_assumptions true, unpinned. That is the shipped configuration, which is what the question is about, but it means the archived configs inherit those defaults rather than stating them, on the usual terms in experiments/README.md.

results.merge_verification: merge_experiments.py's own check: 960 merged rows, 960 distinct keys, 480 from each host, every source row present exactly once.

all_pairs.note: confounded with yield; see the caveat

consequences.config_vintage: The key did not exist before this campaign, so no config archived under experiments/ can state it and every one of them now inherits mrs. Reproducing any earlier campaign therefore needs status_grading = "tiered" written in by hand. This is the widest config-vintage change recorded so far, because it swaps the status objective for a different function rather than shifting a threshold: tiered scores every unrealizable candidate 0.5, where mrs spreads that region over a fraction, so selection sees a gradient the archived campaign never had. Recorded in experiments/README.md under 'Config vintage'. This campaign is the one exception, since sweep G writes the key into both arms.
consequences.reinterpretation: A zero-yield row from an archived TLSF campaign on the arbiter or rg families now reads as a property of the tiered scale rather than of the search. Combined with the ltlsynt-budget change above, amba's archived 96/96 zero-yield is uninformative on two independent counts.
